utterances.text: Yes, I do. He was the third member of General Morillon's tight little party.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit D231 now, please. Oh, I understand it's under seal. So as long as it's not placed on the ELMO, that's not a problem. I'm in fact not going to ask about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. It depends on what your question's going to be, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The questions only involve the means by which this was transmitted, which I think is acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You can show it to the witness without it being put on the ELMO and you can put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply this: Do you see that in this document on the first page there's a report by you sent by TacSat?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That is a secure method of communication?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Particularly because I was transmitting grid zones over the radio and I did not want people to hear that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And on the same page, we see that Major Tucker sent a report by HF. Now, what is HF?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: HF is a form of radio communication, high frequency. And it's basically a bounce system where you bounce it off the atmosphere and it comes down to another location.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that a secure method of communication?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: In this case, no, it was not secure. This was the standard UNPROFOR method of communication in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So the Serbs could have access to this sitrep with all the details?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was that good military practice?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Lousy military practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, actually, I'm finished with that -- that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you talk much with Major Tucker when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: No, we communicated very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What sort of relations did you have with him?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: To be honest, not very good. He wasn't very good about communicating to the rest of the team General Morillon's intentions and or was going to be happening next. It was a rather frustrating situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever have problems with him regarding the radio?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Yes, let me relate one incident. And this is the same pallet that we were having dropped to re-supply our forces within Srebrenica, and this is where we had the typhoid medicine and the batteries. I knew it was coming in and I needed a vehicle to go secure the supplies immediately. He was on the radio sending a report or talking or something, and I was begging him to get off of it so I could take this vehicle to recover the supplies, and he would not do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was there any other way in which he possibly alienated either you or others in the team?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: He was a stand-offish individual. And, again, as I stated, he was the aid to General Morillon, particularly since he spoke fluent French, and he was the senior military man on the ground after General Morillon, particularly being his aid. We were all working for General Morillon, and we did not get General Morillon's intentions briefed to us. So we were left in the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From that document we've just seen, it appears that two majors on the ground were both sending independent reports. Is that correct and is that good practice?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: No -- that is correct, and no, it is not good practice. You usually want to coordinate your reports, so you're speaking with one tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think you've described how at one point you were left as a senior officer without being forewarned?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you provide Major Tucker with much information?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Initially I attempted to. That's a good standard military practice, but then after a while I found him very uncommunicative and I just sort of gave up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever tell him any stories about Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: No. None that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you hear -- ever hear anything negative about Naser Oric when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: No, I did not. I would like to state to you what I did hear, if that is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I'm dealing specifically with this issue, and I want to take it step by step. Was Major Tucker a reliable source of information for you?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, will you give me one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a fairly lengthy final section, but I prefer to deal with it all in one go, so I would actually prefer to finish early today and I can finish within 20 minutes, half an hour at a maximum tomorrow. It's just that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have 20 minutes now, if you want, if you think you can finish in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't. That's why I say half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. If you require 30 minutes, then obviously you won't be able to do that today. Tomorrow morning I suppose you know already that we will be starting at 8.00 and not 9.00. You have been informed about that. Sir, you know about that, too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You think you will be in a position to finish your cross-examination tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intended to do the cross-examination within one day. It just depends on a couple of issues that are raised and I'll have to consult with the team. But that's my intention. It might go over very briefly into the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we adjourn here. Thank you so much, Lieutenant Colonel. We'll see you again tomorrow morning at 8.00. And I think -- you need to decide whether you will need Tony Birtley here tomorrow or you start with him the day after. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think probably -- well, I'll consider that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of December, 2005, at 8.00 a.m.
